questions.q: Which step in order to cash creates the customer receivable in FI?
questions.reason: Billing creates the accounting document that debits the customer and credits revenue and output VAT. The sales order is only a promise and posts nothing.

questions.q: Does saving the sales order (VA01) post anything to the general ledger?
options: No, it is a promise to deliver; it may check credit and reserve stock
questions.reason: The sales order posts nothing in FI. Postings start with goods issue and billing.

questions.q: What does the goods issue for the 10 tables post?
options: Debit cost of goods sold, credit finished goods inventory
questions.reason: When the tables leave the warehouse their value leaves stock and becomes cost of goods sold.

questions.q: What is the gross invoice amount to Hygge Hjem?
questions.reason: 10 tables × DKK 12,000 = 120,000 net, plus 25% VAT of 30,000, gives 150,000.

questions.q: Which posting does billing on 15.03 create?
options: Debit 140000 Receivables 150,000; credit 800000 Revenue 120,000; credit 175000 Output VAT 30,000
questions.reason: The customer owes the gross amount (debit), and revenue and the VAT owed to SKAT are credited.

questions.q: With terms of 14 days net and an invoice dated 15.03, when is the invoice due?
questions.reason: 15.03 plus 14 days is 29.03.

questions.q: What is a reconciliation account such as 140000?
options: The GL account that automatically collects the total of all customer balances
A bank account used for incoming payments
An account only used at year-end
questions.reason: Every customer posting also updates the reconciliation account named on the BP; you never post to it directly.

questions.q: In S/4HANA, how is a customer such as Hygge Hjem maintained?
options: As a Business Partner (transaction BP) with customer roles
Only in a separate customer table with its own transaction
questions.reason: In S/4HANA customers and suppliers are Business Partners with roles such as FI customer.

questions.q: How does SAP know to post the base price to 800000 Sales revenue?
options: Revenue account determination maps SD condition types to GL accounts
The billing clerk types the account on every invoice
It always posts to the first revenue account in the chart
questions.reason: Consultants set up rules that map condition types (and things like customer group) to GL accounts.

questions.q: A billing document exists but there is no accounting document. What is a common cause?
options: It is blocked for transfer to accounting, often due to an account determination error
The credit limit was too high
questions.reason: If SAP cannot find an account, the billing document is not released to accounting until the rule is fixed.

questions.q: What is the +71 FI-kort payment ID used for?
options: To let SAP find the right invoice automatically when the payment arrives
questions.reason: The payment ID printed on the invoice comes back on the bank statement, so SAP can match the payment to the open item.

questions.q: Which transaction imports the electronic bank statement (camt.053 or MT940)?
questions.reason: FF_5 loads the statement and posts what it can match. F150 is dunning, VF01 billing, FBL5N line items.

questions.q: A bank statement line has no usable reference. Where is it handled?
options: In FEBAN, bank statement post-processing, where a clerk finds and clears the item
It is sent back to the bank automatically
questions.reason: The bank side posts, but the customer side waits in FEBAN until someone matches it.

questions.q: What should the balance of 113100 Bank incoming clearing be after all payments are matched?
options: The same as the bank balance
questions.reason: It is a waiting room: debit when the bank side posts, credit when the customer is cleared. A growing balance means unmatched payments.

questions.q: What does F-28 do?
options: Posts an incoming payment by hand and clears the selected open items
questions.reason: F-28 is the manual incoming payment screen, for example for a cheque or when the bank file fails.

questions.q: Hygge Hjem pays DKK 100,000 and the clerk uses the residual item method. What is open afterwards?
options: A new item of DKK 50,000; the original invoice is cleared
The original invoice of 150,000 plus a payment of 100,000
questions.reason: Residual item clears the invoice and creates a new open item for what is still owed.

questions.q: Hygge Hjem pays DKK 100,000 and the clerk uses partial payment. What is open afterwards?
options: The original invoice of 150,000 and the payment of 100,000, linked
questions.reason: With a partial payment the invoice stays open with its due date, and the payment is added as a linked open item.

questions.q: A customer pays DKK 50 short because of a bank fee, and that is inside the tolerance. What happens?
options: The difference is written off automatically and the invoice is cleared
A dunning letter is sent at once
questions.reason: Payment difference tolerances let small differences be written off automatically.

questions.q: With terms of 2% within 8 days, how much would Hygge Hjem pay on the DKK 150,000 invoice if they paid in time?
questions.reason: 2% of the gross 150,000 is 3,000, so they pay 147,000.

questions.q: Of a DKK 3,000 cash discount on a gross amount with 25% VAT, how much is VAT?
questions.reason: The VAT share of a gross amount at 25% is 25/125 = 20%, so 600 is VAT and 2,400 is net.

questions.q: Hygge Hjem overpays by DKK 1,000. What usually happens?
options: The invoice is cleared and 1,000 stays as a credit on the customer's account
The whole payment is sent back
The extra is booked as revenue
questions.reason: An overpayment leaves a credit that can be refunded or used against the next invoice.

questions.q: A credit memo for one scratched table (DKK 12,000 net) is posted. What does Hygge Hjem then owe?
Which transaction runs dunning in classic SAP FI-AR?
questions.reason: F150 creates a dunning proposal, which is checked, and then prints the reminders.

questions.q: Under the Danish Interest Act as described in the lesson, what is the minimum gap between fee-bearing reminders?
questions.reason: The lesson says at least 10 days between reminders, with fees capped. Always confirm current rules with legal or finance.

questions.q: What does DSO measure?
options: How many days of sales are waiting to be paid on average
The number of dunning letters sent
questions.reason: DSO is receivables ÷ sales × days. In the example, 300,000 ÷ 1,350,000 × 90 = 20 days.

questions.q: After the 27.03 payment, what is the balance of 175000 Output VAT from this sale?
questions.reason: The payment clears the receivable, not the VAT. The 30,000 is still owed to SKAT with the VAT return.

questions.q: Hygge Hjem has DKK 150,000 open and a DKK 500,000 credit limit. What happens to a new order of DKK 400,000?
options: It is blocked for a credit check, because 550,000 exceeds the limit
It reduces the credit limit to 100,000
questions.reason: Open receivables plus the new order (550,000) exceed the 500,000 limit, so SAP Credit Management blocks it.

questions.q: What is the difference between a bad debt provision and a write-off?
options: A provision books the expected loss while the item stays open; a write-off clears the item as lost
A provision clears the item; a write-off keeps it open
questions.reason: Provisions are for doubtful debts; write-offs are for debts that are definitely lost.
